question.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}x+2y=3 \\ \frac{1}{6}x-\frac{2}{3}y=-7\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second equation by $6,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14221742/assets/660b0d2d2fc46ff0ef6121ee63d88696bf0b977a80733eece86e8b2937f55994.svg)

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $y$ by adding the two equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+\cancel{4y} & =6 \\ x-\cancel{4y} & =-42 \\ (5x+x) & =(6-42) \\ 6x & =-36 \\ x & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-6$ into the second equation to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x-4y & =-42 \\ -6-4y & =-42 \\ -4y & =-36 \\ y & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=-6$ and $y=9.$
